page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Below the text: the closing line "FINIS ARCHELOGIÆ." and, at lower right, the catchword. The strip of text at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

l.i: tibi gratias, ô Deus, ô principium principiorum, pro
bonis illis donis, quæ in nos ubertim confers nil tale
merentes. Magnum est, ô magne Deus, quòd aperuisti
nobis Scholam naturæ, in quâ das nobis librum, quo te-
ipsum manifestas, & accendis lumen, quo evolvimus
istum librum discussis tenebris & nebulis mentis.
Majus est, ô magne Pater, quòd aperuisti nobis Scho-
lam Gratiæ, in quâ das nobis librum Scripturæ, in quo
tuam voluntatem de nobis & à nobis discimus,
& accendis lumen Gratiæ, quo freti legere possu-
mus librum illum. Maximum denique est, ô maxime
Pater, quòd nos tandem aliquando deduces in Scho-
lam Gloriæ, ubi scientia sine disciplinâ, finis sine fine,
collatio sine decessione, receptio sine accessione, quies
sine motu, triumphus sine bello. Gratias igitur tibi
agimus immortales, ô gratiose, ô gloriose, ô immor-
talis Deus, pro tantis hisce beneficiis. Rogamus te, Cle-
mentissime Pater, præbe Ecclesiis & Scholis halcyo-
nia, adversus Satanam & administros ejus, & nobis
in iis. Benedic vitæ, valetudini, studiis, & laboribus
nostris. Duc nos viâ rectâ ad metam, quæ nobis in
cælo reservatur ad divinæ tuæ gratiæ gloriam, per Do-
minum nostrum Jesum Christum, qui tecum & cum
Spiritu sancto regnat & vivit, Deus benedictus
in omne ævum, Amen Amen! Etiam
Domine Jesu!

page.notes: The "Maximum denique" word shows a superscript mark after "deniq", read here as "denique" with the e-abbreviation uncertain. The catchword "JOH-" is set at the lower right below the last line, as printed. Greek and other scripts: none on this page. The right-edge strip is show-through or the neighbouring page and was not transcribed.
